## Context / Problem

`tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth_jwks.py::test_rejects_bad_claims[mint_kwargs3]` fails whenever more than 1 hour passes between test collection and the moment the test runs.

The cause is the parametrize list (lines 165-173). Its `nbf` and `exp` values are computed with `int(time.time())` when pytest imports the module, not when the test runs.

Observed on 2026-11-03 in a `make verify` run in fix-slug2 that took 4 h 58 min on a host with load average about 40:
- The parametrized `nbf` was 1793758291, which is collection time plus 3600 s.
- The token was minted later, at about 1793760867: its default `exp` of 1793764467 is mint time plus 3600 s.
- By then `nbf` was already in the past, so the verifier accepted the "not yet valid" token, and the test's assertion that it is `None` failed.
- In isolation the module passes 3 out of 3 runs.

The `exp` case (`mint_kwargs2`) has the same flaw, but there time only makes the token more expired, so that case stays correct by luck.

### Reproduction (2026-11-03)

Importing the module with `time.time` shifted 2 h into the past, then running each parametrized case on the real clock, makes the `nbf` case accept the token in 3 of 3 runs; the other 3 cases stay rejected.

Patching `time.time` FORWARD between collection and the call does NOT reproduce it (all 4 cases rejected on the unfixed code): the token is minted with `time.time`, but PyJWT validates `nbf`/`exp` against `datetime.now()`, so only the minting clock moves and `nbf` stays in the verifier's future. A test built that way passes on the broken code and cannot prove the fix, so the acceptance criterion below shifts the collection clock instead.

### Survey of the test tree

An AST scan of `tests/**/*.py` for clock calls (`time.time`, `time_ns`, `monotonic`, `perf_counter`, `datetime.now`/`utcnow`, `date.today`) evaluated at module level, class level, in decorators, or in argument defaults finds only lines 171-172 of this file; a text grep for module-level clock assignments (incl. `gmtime`/`localtime`/`strftime`) finds none. No other site shares the cause.

## Approach

Compute the claim values at test time. Each parametrized case becomes a function of the current time (`lambda now: {"nbf": now + 3600}`), with explicit ids, and the test body calls it with `int(time.time())`.

Add a regression test in the same module that loads a fresh, separate copy of the module (via `importlib.util`, not registered in `sys.modules`) with `time.time` shifted 2 h into the past, patches `jwt.PyJWKClient` with the copy's fake client, and runs the copy's `test_rejects_bad_claims` for every parametrized case on the real clock. No autouse fixture and no subprocess.

## File impact

- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth_jwks.py` (only file changed)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The time-relative claim values of `test_rejects_bad_claims` are computed in the test body. A regression test proves this: with the module collected under a clock 2 h in the past and the cases run on the real clock, the not-yet-valid (`nbf`) case still asserts rejection; that regression test fails on the unfixed code.
- [ ] `pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_auth_jwks.py` passes.
